newsitem.title: UK: Dutch TNT bid worries British post office.
newsitem.headline: Dutch TNT bid worries British post office.

text.p: The chief executive of Britain's Post Office said on Wednesday that he was worried that the bid by its Dutch equivalent for Australian company TNT Ltd would give it a stepping stone into the British postal market.
Dutch PTT Post BV earlier this month offered 2.45 Australian dollars per ordinary share for TNT in a deal valuing the company at about $2.0 billion.

John Roberts told parliament's trade and industry committee that he was concerned that post offices in European countries other than Britain "are all becoming much freer to develop different services, to go into partnerships and joint ventures".
On the Dutch attempt to acquire TNT, he added: "If that bid goes through there will be no reason why the Dutch Post Office should not operate in the UK in the deregulated area."

The deregulated area at present consists of mail costing at least one stg to deliver, a Post Office spokesman said. However, he noted European Commission proposals to deregulate other areas, such as circulars.
Roberts said the British post office was at present not allowed to go into partnership with, or take over, commercial firms, putting it at a competitive disadvantage.
